title: Recurring unresolved limitation 'residual-confounding' across 3 independent papers
explanation: 3 independent papers (2013–2024) report an own-work limitation normalized to 'residual-confounding'. Mixed-fidelity: 3 full-text, 0 abstract-only; score corrected for the ~11x full-text detection bias = 0.600 vs uncorrected 0.600. Methodological diversity: 3 distinct methods (NOTE: diversity/time-span weighting extends beyond opportunity-criteria.md). Resolution is ASSUMED absent — no limitation-resolution relation exists in Phase 3, so 'unresolved' is unverified. Example limitation statements: Residual confounding from unmeasured behavioral factors or imprecision in covariate measurement cannot be rule | Observational epidemiological studies included in the review have inherent risk of residual confounding. | Because evidence was pooled from observational prospective cohort studies, unmeasured and residual confounding. Papers: openalex:W2122520859; openalex:W2946931470; openalex:W4392600894.

consumer.headline: 3 separate teams ran into the same wall: residual confounding
consumer.kind_short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
consumer.kind_long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.
consumer.strength_meaning: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
consumer.why: 3 separate research teams each reported hitting this in their own work. They did not build on each other, so this is unlikely to be one group's bad luck. Their papers span 1 years. We could read 3 of them in full, which is where teams describe what actually went wrong.
